gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Styro crowds its letters shoulder to shoulder, with barely a gap left in the e and c, and the retro swagger comes from that squeeze. Noto Sans Coptic is the opposite, a plain sans whose open s and c let the middle of each line carry the text.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Retro and tightly packed, Styro pinches its e and c nearly shut. Then Noto Sans Cuneiform swells into round, glassy lowercase with an open e, and that gap between squeezed and inflated is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Styro packs its lowercase large and tight, the e and c nearly sealed. Noto Sans Deseret reads wide and low with squat ascenders, and its open apertures keep a long stretch of text easy on the eye.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Noto Sans Devanagari reads compact, its capitals melting into the lowercase and its g leaving the lower curve open. Styro, meanwhile, jams its letters together, so a longer passage feels like slipping from a crowded room into open air.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Styro presses its big retro letters so close that the e and c barely open at all. Noto Sans Duployan answers with oversized, wide-mouthed counters.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Styro's crowded, nearly closed e and c give it a retro bark. It excels at that commanding punch, while Noto Sans Elbasan does the quieter work, with large lowercase and open terminals that never pinch shut.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic keeps every aperture open and its ascenders barely above the x-height. Noto Sans Elymaic against Styro makes a clear split on the page: Styro's retro letters sit jammed together while the sans breathes.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Noto Sans Ethiopic stands tall and sturdy, its c terminals hanging far from the bowl. Styro earns its keep big and brief, where its crowded, retro letters can hit hard before the open sans takes over.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Styro's letters crowd together until the e and c barely show a gap, which gives it a retro, commanding stance. Yet Noto Sans Georgian opens every curve and keeps its ascender stems short, so the two feel tight against loose.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Tight, retro and a bit bossy, Styro nearly seals its e and c. But Noto Sans Glagolitic is the plain sans that lets round, sturdy letters read clearly, so one handles the shout and the other the sentences.
